clinicalPearls: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by mutations in NEFL, encoding neurofilament light chain, and notable as a demyelinating-range phenotype produced by an axonal cytoskeletal protein.
NEFL mutations are allelic: the same gene causes both demyelinating CMT1F and axonal CMT2E, and many patients show intermediate conduction that blurs the CMT1 and CMT2 divide.
Usually autosomal dominant, though recessive and de novo cases occur, and early-onset, more severe childhood presentations are recognised.
Core features are typical of CMT: distal weakness, wasting, pes cavus, distal sensory loss and areflexia.
Some patients present in early childhood with delayed motor milestones, and sensory involvement can be prominent.
Nerve conduction may show slowed velocities in the demyelinating range despite the underlying axonal and neuronal pathology.
Diagnosis rests on identifying a pathogenic NEFL variant; labelling as CMT1F versus CMT2E depends on the conduction phenotype.
Exclude the far commoner CMT1A (PMP22 duplication) before or alongside broader sequencing.
reference.pathophysiology: NEFL encodes neurofilament light chain, the smallest of the three neurofilament subunits that co-assemble into the neuronal intermediate-filament cytoskeleton essential for axonal calibre and axonal transport. Dominant, typically missense, mutations disrupt neurofilament assembly, cause abnormal aggregation and impair transport of neurofilaments and organelles along the axon. The consequent axonal dysfunction is accompanied by secondary changes in myelination, which is why the same gene can present with demyelinating-range slow conduction (CMT1F), axonal conduction (CMT2E) or an intermediate pattern. The disorder therefore illustrates how a primarily axonal, neuron-intrinsic defect can generate a phenotype that electrophysiologically resembles a demyelinating neuropathy.
additionalDifferentials: CMT2E, the axonal counterpart caused by the same NEFL gene
CMT1A (PMP22 duplication) and other demyelinating CMT1 subtypes (MPZ, GJB1, EGR2)
Dominant intermediate CMT (for example YARS1, MPZ)
Acquired chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy as a treatable mimic
Early-onset or severe childhood hereditary neuropathy of Dejerine-Sottas phenotype
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography to define a demyelinating, axonal or intermediate pattern
Gene panel or exome sequencing including NEFL
Family segregation analysis and pedigree review, considering de novo and recessive inheritance
PMP22 dosage testing to exclude the common CMT1A duplication
Clinical genetics referral and genetic counselling
Developmental and functional assessment in early-onset paediatric cases
redFlags: Rapidly progressive or relapsing course suggesting acquired inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy
Conduction block or marked temporal dispersion, which is atypical for inherited disease
Severe early-onset weakness with respiratory or bulbar involvement
Central nervous system signs prompting consideration of a broader neurofilament-related phenotype
reference.prognosis: The course ranges from a typical slowly progressive CMT to more severe early-onset disease with greater disability; most patients retain ambulation and life expectancy is generally normal, although early-onset cases tend to be more disabling.
pitfalls: Being misled by demyelinating-range conduction velocities into excluding an axonal-gene cause such as NEFL.
Treating CMT1F and CMT2E as unrelated entities when they are allelic and can coexist within families.
Not testing for the far commoner CMT1A duplication before broader sequencing.
Missing a treatable inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy in atypical or rapidly progressive presentations.
Overlooking de novo variants in apparently sporadic early-onset cases.
management: Manage supportively with physiotherapy and occupational therapy, as there is no disease-modifying treatment
Provide ankle-foot orthoses, podiatry, footwear and walking aids for foot drop and pes cavus
Provide intensive paediatric rehabilitation and developmental support for severe early-onset childhood presentations
Offer orthopaedic foot surgery for fixed disabling deformity and treat neuropathic pain symptomatically, avoiding neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine
Monitor progression and functional status, screening for scoliosis in early-onset disease
Offer genetic counselling that accounts for the dominant, recessive and de novo inheritance of NEFL variants, and assess relatives accordingly
Coordinate multidisciplinary neuromuscular, orthopaedic and rehabilitation care
